operations.evidence: The first-receptions table for former armed-services members was paused indefinitely after a data-quality investigation.
Suspended data must not be promoted or used to infer outcomes.
There were 56,923 releases from custody in 2025: 56,581 from determinate sentences and 342 from indeterminate sentences.
Release totals are national justice-system flows, not neighbourhood safety measures.
Determinate-sentence releases in 2025 were virtually unchanged from 2024 and remained below the 2015 to 2019 average.
Trend comparisons do not provide event or parcel geography.
Releases from determinate sentences over six months and under 12 months increased by 35% to 8,491 in 2025.
The change is associated with sentencing policy and cannot be attributed to a property.
There were 342 releases from indeterminate sentences in 2025, 23% fewer than in 2024.
The figure is a national flow and not a local safety signal.
For determinate releases in 2025, mean sentence length was 27.6 months and mean time served was 14.3 months.
Averages conceal variation and cannot be applied to individuals or locations.
For determinate releases in 2025, median sentence length was 14.0 months and median time served was 6.0 months.
Medians are aggregate descriptors and not parcel-level inputs.
There were 11,796 Home Detention Curfew releases in 2025, 16% more than in 2024.
HDC releases reflect eligibility and policy changes, not local incident risk.
Prisoners serving determinate sentences of four years or more accounted for 33% of HDC releases in 2025, compared with 23% in 2024.
The share is a release-policy measure and not spatial evidence.
Of offenders released on HDC in 2024, 21% were recalled, compared with 19% in the previous year.
The latest complete HDC recall cohort lags the release period and cannot be used for parcel scoring.
There were 383,197 releases-on-temporary-licence incidences in 2025, 5% fewer than in 2024.
ROTL incidences may include repeated events for the same person and have no parcel geography.
The number of individuals receiving temporary licence fell by 7% to 7,154 in 2025.
The person count is national and cannot indicate local risk.
Prisoner-transfer incidences increased by 4% to 95,247, while people receiving at least one transfer increased by 3% to 66,471.
Transfers reflect operational movement and must not be interpreted as local crime events.
There were 14,643 releases in October to December 2025: 14,555 determinate and 88 indeterminate.
The quarterly release count is not local public-safety evidence.
